meta.title: FULL EPISODE: Chris Camillo Reveals The Next ULTIMATE Trade Of 2026
meta.thread_line: 6 threads · Take-Two/GTA VI long · GTA side trades · Optimus stalled, Apple missing robots · Amazon dip-buying · vibes market · new media vs scrolling

snapshot: Camillo's biggest live trade is a **long in Take-Two (TTWO)** into the GTA VI launch, with millions in equity and a possible $1M options trade; his edge claim is that almost nobody is running scenario math.
His bull case rests on **depth of gameplay interest**: if monetization lands near $60 per monthly active user on 50-60M+ players, he sees the stock doubling.
He calls Tesla's **Optimus program 'in shambles'** and says the stock is now a robot-execution bet he no longer trusts; self-driving is mostly priced in and the moat is thinner.
Apple: **no position, no strong feelings**; the one thing that would excite him is an embodied-AI home robot, where Apple's trust and ecosystem are unmatched.

Amazon: exited the weekly-call position, kept a smaller levered stake, and says he will **relever on dips** that come from non-structural news; half-point rate moves don't matter against AI-driven growth.
His read of the market: **'vibes' investing** dominates, so being right early may not move the price (GoPro/Markiplier is the example).
Biggest unreachable bet: **new media**, the layer between podcasting and TV; both sides also admit short-form scrolling is a brain-rot problem and swap fixes.

themes.status: LONG — MILLIONS IN EQUITY, MAY ADD OPTIONS
themes.title: Take-Two: the GTA VI trade is about gameplay depth and online monetization
themes.lead: Camillo is long Take-Two because first gameplay suggests unit sales at or above the high end of the 30-50M range and a path to billions a year from online.
bullets: Sell-side calendar-year-1 unit estimates run **30-50M**; based on the first 27 minutes of gameplay he expects the high end or beyond.
Monetization is the swing factor: **$20 vs $60 per monthly active user** — near $60 on 50-60M+ users, he sees Take-Two stock doubling.
He models **$2-3B a year** from GTA VI Online microtransactions, on top of 50-60M copies at ~$90-100 (most buyers take the $100 edition).
Precedent: GTA V still generates ~$600M a year in microtransactions, 13 years after launch; GTA V Online arrived ~17 days after the console release, so he doubts a rumored 2-year online delay.

Sensor Tower's ~4.8M pre-sales figure is its first console estimate (methodology unknown); he calls it unsurprising for a digital-only game, vs ~7M hard-copy pre-orders for GTA V in 2013. Take-Two called early pre-orders 'unprecedented'.
Sentiment read: he went through ~30,000 organic comments on the Netflix trailer and rates the gameplay reveal a 10/10; negatives about story don't hold because none was shown.
Risk he names himself: timing. He can't say when others will notice, and a miss on the holiday release window would hurt the stock badly.

quote.text: I don't play the game, but I play the stock.

themes.watch: He traded Take-Two's GTA launches back in 1999 and has a position here; the Netflix-trailer comment sample and 27 minutes of gameplay are his own sentiment read, and he says gameplay depth is 'yet to be determined'.

names.name: Take-Two Interactive (TTWO)
names.blurb: Owner of Rockstar; GTA VI launch is the catalyst. Millions in equity; considering a ~$1M options trade; goal of $1M+ profit.

themes.title: GTA side trades: delivery apps up, entertainment and dating down
themes.lead: A 60-day gaming window should lift delivery and could drain time and spending elsewhere, but Camillo still says the main trade is Take-Two.
bullets: Delivery: he sees DoorDash benefiting, probably Uber Eats too; roughly a third of GTA gamers are in the US, two-thirds abroad.
Hosts floated shorts or losers: Barnes & Noble, dating apps, and movie studios (some are already warning of lower viewership).
Hosts' picks for adjacent demand: energy drinks, chairs, monitors.
Cultural framing: GTA is the most cross-generational game ever and a rare shared event, like Halo Tuesday or the Adrian's Kickback meetup; he links it to male loneliness.
No GTA 7 expected: they'll use AI to expand the GTA universe over a decade rather than spend another 13 years on one build.
He plans a GTA delivery special at his Dallas restaurants; as a bit, he reserved the Nevada plate 'GTA IRL' (guess: ~$5K resale).
themes.watch: He owns a restaurant group that would benefit from the GTA delivery special he describes.

names.blurb: Expected to see heavy GTA-night ordering.

themes.status: TESLA THESIS RESET; APPLE: NO POSITION
themes.title: Optimus is stalled and Apple has missed embodied AI
themes.lead: Camillo's old Tesla bull case was the Optimus robot, and his intel says it is far behind; Apple, he argues, is the one firm that could win the home robot and isn't trying.
bullets: Tesla: his only thesis was Optimus (once imagined as a ~$10 trillion division); two-plus years of intel say talent loss, friction with Elon, and unresolved hand strategy.
A promised public Optimus update for March-April this year never came; he says it isn't ready for scale.
He disputes an influencer claiming Optimus is a year and a half ahead of every other robot; his intel says the opposite.
Self-driving: Tesla may lead on robotaxi cost, but he sees Waymo and Chinese rivals (also exporting) closing in, so he won't pay up for it.
Apple: new CEO's $56M pay package is nonmaterial to him; he's neutral and owns none, seeing a cash cow with no clear 5-year growth driver.
Home robots are his Apple hope: trust, closed ecosystem and personal data are unique, yet his intel is that its robot program was 'an arm in a box' and the car team moved to robotics.
He sees embodied AI as potentially larger than AI, with big moats; commercial and home markets are each multi-trillion-dollar sectors.

quote.text: The Optimus program has been in shambles.

themes.watch: Optimus claims come from his own private intel, which he doesn't source; a Tesla fan view on Optimus progress would differ.

names.name: Tesla (TSLA)
names.blurb: Optimus execution is the only thesis; behind schedule per his intel. Self-driving priced in.

names.name: Apple (AAPL)
names.blurb: Not excited; no position. Would get interested if a home-robot program emerged.

themes.status: HOLDING — SMALLER LEVERED STAKE, ADDING ON DIPS
themes.title: Amazon: dips on non-structural news are entries, not exits
themes.lead: Camillo is out of his weekly calls but still levered, and plans to relever heavily within months because the stock keeps falling on noise.
bullets: Amazon beat earnings, popped, then slid back to pre-earnings levels; he calls it the 'perfect representation of the modern investor' — too big to promise 3-10x, so it's unsexy.
Decision rule: he looks at what's driving the drop. A story that doesn't change the long term gets bought; a meaningful one gets a reassessment and maybe a trim.
Latest drop #1: a North Carolina lawsuit alleging Amazon widened ad-auction bid spreads, with ~$20B potentially taken from advertisers; he expects years of litigation and a settlement.
Latest drop #2: a higher-than-expected 10-year yield; he thinks half-point moves are meaningless against growth accelerating from ~11% a year and a half ago to ~16% next year on the AI cycle.
He admits borrowing cost and the opportunity cost of risk assets both rise with rates, but says investors are reacting from 20 years of muscle memory.
themes.watch: He is personally long and levered; he says he'll lighten if the news turns structural.

names.name: Amazon (AMZN)
names.blurb: Exited weekly calls, kept smaller levered stake, adding on dips, big relever planned.

themes.title: The vibes market: GoPro, Markiplier and why being right early may not pay
themes.lead: Camillo argues today's retail flow trades on narrative, not benchmarks, which breaks the usual 'do the work, get paid' loop.
bullets: Hosts argued GTA hype is already priced to infinity; Camillo counters that 'baked in' is never quantified (30M? 40M? 50M units? what year-1 ARPU?).
In 1999-2000 traders had structural unit and beat/miss benchmarks; now many buyers and shorts of Take-Two don't know the sell-side unit forecasts.
GoPro: 'just vibes'. He bought ~$40K to hedge FOMO and sold for roughly a slight profit.
Markiplier disclosed an 8.5% GoPro stake when its market cap was ~$60M (roughly $5-8M invested), and it reportedly grew to ~$20M; Camillo reads it as a publicity play.
Build-A-Bear: a huge pandemic-era trade for him; he wanted to merge it with collectibles, Crocs-style collabs and limited releases, but didn't want the CEO job again.

quote.text: The market is dumber than it's ever been because everybody has a strong opinion, but so few people, less than ever, are actually willing to do the real work.

themes.watch: His own Take-Two position benefits if the vibe-driven crowd catches up to his thesis; he concedes he's 'maybe totally wrong, but informed'.

names.name: GoPro (GPRO)
names.blurb: Small ~$40K FOMO trade, sold; meme-style run led by Markiplier's 8.5% stake.

names.name: Build-A-Bear (BBW)
names.blurb: Past pandemic trade; thinks one hit product moves it and it needs better collabs.

themes.title: New media is the market he'd buy if he could; short-form is the cost
themes.lead: Camillo's biggest unreachable bet is new-media content creators, while all agree short-form scrolling is damaging and trade fixes.
bullets: Thesis: a next phase of media sits between podcasting 1.0 ('two guys and a mic') and TV; top creators gain value as old-media firms buy in over the next 5 years.
He also names private embodied AI as something most people can't invest in.
Nobody watches TV anymore beyond sports and viral Netflix shows; one host can't get 10 minutes into a series before returning to TikTok.
He scrolls for market research (consumer behavior, spending, attention) and admits it's addictive and he overdoes it.
Fixes: keep a black-and-white phone filter outside intentional use, time-box research (e.g. 10pm-2am), meditate or journal around people without phones, vary routines so life doesn't 'compress'.
Host forecast: society will look back on shorts like cigarettes, with a split between people raised on shorts and those who weren't.

takeaways.title: Track Take-Two's GTA VI launch date, any delay news and first-month unit disclosures; they decide his thesis.
Replace 'priced in' with explicit unit and ARPU scenarios before taking a side on a hype stock.
Treat Tesla as an Optimus-execution call; wait for a real public demo before leaning on it.
On Amazon, sort each drop into noise or structural before reacting; he buys the former.
Try a grayscale phone filter and a fixed research window to cut mindless scrolling.
Follow new-media creators and acquisitions; it is his top theme he can't directly own.
